question_text: What are androgens? Which cells secrete them?

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What they are
steps.why: Androgens drive the male secondary sexual characters, which is why they are grouped together under one name.
common_mistakes: Naming oestrogen. That is a female sex hormone.
steps.memory_tip: Andro means male: androgens are the male sex hormones.
lines: Androgens are the male sex hormones.

steps.label: Which cells make them
steps.why: The Leydig cells sit between the sperm-making tubules, so the hormone is made right beside the cells it supports.
common_mistakes: Naming Sertoli cells. Those nourish the sperm.
steps.memory_tip: Leydig cells lie between the tubules and make testosterone.
steps.margin_note: Name the cells and where they are.

lines.text: Leydig cells of the testes secrete them

insider_note: Name the cells, not just the testis. Leydig cells is the marked answer.
